title: Nomograms for the prognosis prediction model of early-stage triple-negative breast cancer - based on SEER database

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Nomograms for the prognosis prediction model of early-stage triple-negative breast cancer - based on SEER database》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · S0001-p5】At present, clinical studies on TNBC drug therapy have yielded encouraging results, and patient survival has been prolonged after comprehensive treatment [16]. Nevertheless, breast cancer mortality remains high, and treatment strategies for TNBC patients still require further investigation. Nomograms can integrate multiple key predictors and estimate an endpoint intuitively and simply, thereby enabling prognostic assessment of patients, particularly those with cancer. By integrating multiple prognostically relevant clinicopathological factors and constructing a prognostic prediction model through visualization and quantitative methods, an objective description of a patient’s prognosis can be obtained, leading to more accurate predictions.

【Background · S0001-p6】Although several prognostic models have been proposed to predict the outcome of breast cancer patients [17–19], most are only partially clinically applicable, primarily to hormone receptor‑positive breast cancer. While several prognostic prediction models exist for TNBC patients [20–22], their complexity and high technical requirements have limited their widespread clinical use. Moreover, studies on nomogram prediction models specifically for early-stage TNBC are still rare. Therefore, in this study we constructed nomograms for disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) using data from early-stage TNBC patients in the SEER database. An external validation cohort was assembled using data from Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), with the aim of better predicting the survival of early-stage TNBC patients and ultimately supporting more accurate clinical decision-making.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Nomograms for the prognosis prediction model of early-stage triple-negative breast cancer - based on SEER database》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Statistical methods · S0002-S2003-p3】The predictive performance of the nomograms was evaluated by calculating the concordance index (C-index), plotting receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calibration curves, and calculating the area under the ROC curve (AUC) using the “rms” package in R. Internal validation was performed using bootstrapping with 1,000 resamples. External validation was conducted using the independent SYSUCC cohort. A two-sided P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

【Statistical methods · S0002-S2003-p5】For external validation, the originally developed nomogram was applied directly to the independent cohort without any recalibration or adjustment. This approach was chosen to rigorously evaluate the model’s transportability and performance in a real-world setting where patient populations may differ from the derivation cohort.

Internal validation was performed using bootstrapping with 1,000 resamples. External validation was conducted using the independent SYSUCC cohort. A two-sided P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

For external validation, the originally developed nomogram was applied directly to the independent cohort without any recalibration or adjustment. This approach was chosen to rigorously evaluate the model’s transportability and performance in a real-world setting where patient populations may differ from the derivation cohort.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Nomograms for the prognosis prediction model of early-stage triple-negative breast cancer - based on SEER database》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】The modeling group included 14,389 patients and the validating group 1,146. Age and seven other factors were independent predictors (P < 0.05) and were incorporated into the nomograms. The C-indices for disease-free survival were 0.884 (95% CI: 0.876-0.892) in the modeling group and 0.686 (95% CI: 0.653-0.719) in the validating group. For overall survival, C-indices were 0.873 (95% CI: 0.863-0.883) and 0.741 (95% CI: 0.702-0.780), respectively.

【Conclusion · S0005-p1】The prognosis of patients with early-stage TNBC is independently associated with age, N stage, TNM stage, histologic grade, and the receipt of plastic surgery and radiotherapy. Notably, the observed association between plastic surgery and an increased risk of local recurrence and metastasis warrants further investigation in future multicenter prospective studies to clarify causality. After rigorous internal and external validation, the nomograms constructed in this study demonstrated good prognostic predictive ability. These models may serve as practical tools to more accurately assess DFS and OS in patients with early-stage TNBC, thereby providing an objective reference for clinical decision-making. However, due to the observational nature of the SEER database, the associations between treatment-related factors (e.g., radiotherapy) and survival should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in prospective studies.
